The candidate intent embeds the actual openQuestions and snapshot.verification_gaps text (plumbed via DomainContext.extras), instructing the proposer to convert each into an explicit, grounded backlog/verification task entry — exactly the finding's recommendedAction ('Convert high-impact gaps into explicit backlog or verification tasks').
advisory_architecture_finding_design.target_selection: Do not fabricate per-question filenames or invent paths. Use one stable, repo-root-relative aggregating doc whose parent exists (docs/agent-backlog.md; or docs/decisions/ when the gap is decision-shaped and that dir already exists). Targets are synthesized by policy, not derived from the (filtered) iterationReadiness evidence path, and the parent-exists check in diff_proposer._target_file_contents_or_empty still applies.
advisory_architecture_finding_design.verification_gate: Replace the bare markdown contract with a backlog gate: (1) test -s target (non-empty); (2) markdown_links resolves with no fabricated/missing links; (3) NEW content assertion — every open-question/gap identifier passed via context appears as a task entry (count/id presence match), rejecting a no-op or boilerplate backlog that ignores the real items. Fail-closed if the expected-items list is empty or unmatched.

advisory_verification_finding_design.candidate_generation: verification.quality-gates.present is positive/informational (gates already exist) and must NOT become a mutation candidate — patching it would fabricate work. It is already consumed as planner context (its commands feed _quality_gate_commands → DomainContext.extras and the intake context block, and are reused by ComponentVerificationDomain via _finding_or_quality_gate_verification). Keep it as context and label its skip 'consumed_as_context'. The actionable sibling, verification.quality-gates.missing (boundary blocks_autonomous_mutation), is correctly not autonomously patchable and should remain recorded-but-blocked.
advisory_verification_finding_design.target_selection: No mutation target. As context it may inform the verification sections of other candidates that DO run (AGENTS.md, docs/runbooks) by supplying the canonical gate command list; it never selects a file of its own.

doc_proposer_failure_note: The rank-1 docs run failed in diff_proposer._validate_changed_markdown because of a checker-vs-authoring mismatch, not a model hallucination. The runbooks finding has target docs/runbooks (no suffix), so _proposal_target_for_evidence_path appends index.md → docs/runbooks/index.md. The prompt instructs the model to use repo-relative paths (docs/index.md, README.md), and it did. But markdown_links._resolve_target (markdown_links.py:190) resolves non-absolute links relative to markdown_path.parent, i.e. docs/runbooks/, yielding docs/runbooks/docs/index.md and docs/runbooks/README.md — both missing. Auto-repair (_unique_suffix_match) couldn't help: the link text 'docs/index.md' is ALREADY the canonical repo path, so there is no better string to substitute; the bug is the resolver, not the text. For root-level docs this never shows because repo-relative == parent-relative. This DOES affect the advisory design: docs/agent-backlog.md lives under docs/, so any repo-relative link it emits (e.g. README.md → resolved as docs/README.md) hits the same failure. Mitigation options: make the resolver also attempt repo-root resolution for repo-relative-looking links, OR place the advisory backlog at repo root, OR constrain the contract to root-absolute '/path' links and same-directory references.

risks: No-op/shallow advisory fixes: the markdown contract accepts any non-empty prose, so a backlog that doesn't reflect the gaps would 'pass'. Mitigation: ship the content-aware backlog gate (id/count presence) before relying on the MVP boundary change in autonomous runs.

Fabrication of facts: a backlog grounded only on a finding title invites invented context. Mitigation: plumb the real openQuestions/verification_gaps content and require source-reference grounding via the existing --require-source-references path.
Nested-doc link breakage: docs/agent-backlog.md will hit the same relative-resolution bug as docs/runbooks/index.md. Mitigation: fix _resolve_target or target repo root before enabling advisory docs.

Mislabeling informational findings as actionable: if the boundary loosening is too broad it could turn verification.quality-gates.present into a spurious candidate. Mitigation: scope the predicate to architecture.* + actionable advisory, and keep an explicit informational-advisory→context route.

Churn / duplicate backlogs across runs: repeated runs could regenerate or duplicate the backlog. Mitigation: the proposal_registry proposal_key/lineage path already dedupes by finding+target+intent_hash; ensure the advisory candidate participates so promoted entries are skipped.
summary: Advisory architecture/verification findings are skipped purely because no proposal domain claims them. Two mechanisms cause this: (1) every single-file domain depends on _target_paths_for_finding, which deliberately drops evidence paths beginning with `iterationReadiness` (proposal_domains.py:317), so these Project-Model findings have zero file targets and DocumentationDomain/GenericFileDomain/ComponentVerificationDomain all return []; (2) ModelLevelDomain already exists to handle target-less architecture findings by writing docs/agent-backlog.md, but its predicate _is_model_level_finding requires boundary == 'safe_to_patch_docs_only' (proposal_domains.py:362) and these findings carry boundary == 'advisory_only', so it bails before its architecture.* branch is reached. Result: registry.first_candidate returns None and both planner and ranker record `no_single_file_target`. The verification.quality-gates.present finding is a different case — it is informational/positive and is already consumed as planner context (its commands flow into _quality_gate_commands → DomainContext.extras and the intake context block), so it should stay context, not become a mutation candidate. Making architecture gaps actionable is a small predicate change for an MVP, but a durable fix requires plumbing the actual openQuestions/verification_gaps content into DomainContext and adding a content-aware backlog gate, because the only gate available to ModelLevelDomain today (the non-empty + links-resolve markdown contract) cannot reject a shallow no-op backlog and is itself broken for nested doc targets.
